verdicts.factCheck: I reran prestate_now.py against https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at Ethereum block 26,488,275 and wrote the result to my scratchpad. For chains 10, 130 and 57073 the portal's AnchorStateRegistry returns respectedGameType 9, gameImpls(9) is 0x19af533cc2a2a55786dcb8672aa5717e64213208 with version 0.8.0, and gameArgs(9) begins with prestate 0x03e5a54835d39c1d83b198314473e1f111c3539c04f65c3e8a9b8ccebe3737c9. The newest type 9 games are now index 21572 on OP Mainnet (proxy 0x8834590b...), index 17872 on Unichain (proxy 0x032ae38b...) and index 2655 on Ink, and each returns that same absolutePrestate(). I downloaded the state file from storage.googleapis.com again. Its sha256 is bf144319ba2108dbd89c1d0677114c5c130320e9cdf3eb80cb422f470c2b3f73 and the gunzipped image hashes the same as the work directory copy, d3be3df5...e588. All 20 sampled 4 KiB pages of text.bin occur in the image, and my own count of andi rX, rY, 0x40 words in the text segment gives 66 in 4,928,204 bytes. The LLVM fix is confirmed through the llvm-commits archive page https://lists.llvm.org/pipermail/llvm-commits/Week-of-Mon-20261109/2098972.html (fetched): commit 0212d77 of 2026-11-14, titled 'Use a proper boolean for the select condition in lowerShift*Parts', says that lowerShiftLeftParts and lowerShiftRightParts used (and Shamt, VT.bits) as the condition. The GitHub issue 235261 and the commit page returned HTTP 403 to curl, so I read the issue only through that archive entry and the cycle 13 verdict.
verdicts.codeCheck: BitMath.mostSignificantBit at src/libraries/BitMath.sol:16-22 runs shr(r, x) with a running r that reaches 64 to 127 and more. TickBitmap.flipTick at src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:73 runs shl(and(tick, 0xff), 1), and TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice at src/libraries/TickMath.sol:142-151 runs shr(127, ...), shr(128, r) and shr(f, r). Every one of these goes through the interpreter's SHL, SHR or SAR handler, so the right check is the one the finding makes on the image. I reran cfg_scan.py on the work directory's text.bin into my scratchpad. The output is identical to cfg_scan.json: 66 sites, 135 zero tests, 1 srl by 6 (which maps 64 to 1), no budget exhausted, and 162 flags that are 161 tainted-argument jalr records and 1 return in $3. The classifier at cfg_scan.py:88-98 marks any other read as FLAG, including xori, ori, addu, sltu, multiplies, shift amounts, stores and register compares, so it errs toward flagging. One gap remained. The scan stops passing taint into direct calls past depth 8 (142 depth-limit events at sites 0x1201322d8 and 0x1201322f8), so 'no read' past that depth had not been shown. I reran those four sites with MAXDEPTH 12 and 20 and a 2,000,000 step budget. Up to depth 20 the only reads are 2 and 4 zero tests, and the other events are stale $8 to $11 passed on to calls, with no arithmetic, store or shift-amount read. I also reran run_real.py on the published image with the cycle 13 emulator. The handlers identify as SAR 0x12006ad70, SHL 0x12006b1a8 and SHR 0x12006b328, and 11,316 targeted, 23,763 battery and 57,792 amount 0 to 300 runs give 0 mismatches and 0 emulator faults, as stated.
verdicts.corrections: The 36 indirect calls are 36 pairs of site and jalr spread over 13 distinct jalr instructions and 4 sites (jalr_args.json). src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:38 is the AND that forms bitPos. The shift in position() is sar(8, ...) at line 37, and the shift by the low 8 bits of a tick is at line 73. The depth 8 limit left 142 call paths unfollowed. My rerun to depth 20 found no read on them, but the static scan is still bounded and assumes the n64 calling convention for jalr callees. The shift handlers were found by pattern and identified by their results, and the dispatch table entry that selects them was not read. The static scan of all 66 sites covers any other handler. Actor governance is correct: an ordinary account can drive the permissionless type 9 game, but the fault only reaches it if governance adopts a new prestate whose build folds the condition into arithmetic.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-704: the wasm module root the three Arbitrum-family rollups enforce, the go-ethereum commit of its replay binary, and that commit's opcode, jump analysis, memory and transient storage code compared with 0e44603.
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_call wasmModuleRoot() (selector 0x8ee1a126) returns 0xc10cd7ec...dc97 on 0x4DCeB440 and 0x23a19d23 (Ethereum) and on 0x508C173d (HyperEVM). https://docs.arbitrum.io/run-arbitrum-node/arbos-releases/arbos61 (fetched) ties that root to consensus-v61. I diffed the saved files. analysis_legacy.go and jumpdests.go are identical. The memory difference is clear() at Free plus reuse of capacity, and those bytes are zero on reuse. Transient storage changes only its map layout. The node's 0e44603 adds an Amsterdam table (DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE, SLOTNUM) that the replay lacks, but eth_call on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc with code 0x4b... returns 'invalid opcode: SLOTNUM', so Amsterdam is not active and the node and the replay run the same table. I could not confirm the f1c5f02 submodule pin myself because the GitHub tree page returned 403. The raw instructions.go at f1c5f02 does exist (HTTP 200).
